rules.text: **"Turn Rework" tag — hands off completely (Florencia, 2026-08-07), all regions.** Any meld carrying a tag whose name matches "turn rework" (case/spacing-insensitive) is invisible to every scheduler: never claimed if unassigned, never assigned to a tech, never scheduled or rescheduled, never touched by compaction. Implemented as a shared `hasTag(m, TURN_REWORK_TAG_RE)` check folded into each region's scope filter (`isSpokaneRepair`, the Tacoma tc68/tc34 filter, `isTriCitiesRepair`) — same idiom as the existing pest/vendor/manual-assignment exclusions, just keyed off a tag instead of an assignee.
never schedule **Sunday, Monday, or Saturday**. Monday is held open as an emergency reserve. Work is booked **Tuesday–Friday** only.
details: "Today" is never used either — except a job whose stated preferred date is today, or a past-due job that needs the soonest slot.

rules.text: roughly **8:00 AM – 5:30 PM Pacific**. Times are stored with the Pacific time-zone offset (e.g. `2026-06-25T09:00:00-07:00`).

**Fill the nearest open days first**, packing densely from 8 AM, then a daily **compaction pass** pulls later jobs into the earliest open slots. Keep about a **30-minute buffer** between jobs and never double-book a tech.
details: Busy time is read from the tech's **entire** calendar (including turns), so it never books on top of an all-day turn.
Compaction is idempotent — once everything is packed, a re-run changes nothing.

rules.text: Emergency / Urgent → High → Normal / Medium → Low.
if a job's scheduled time passes without completion, reschedule it to the next available slot (keeping priority order). Never leave a past-due job unscheduled.

**Emergency / Urgent queue (rewritten 2026-07-28, Tacoma + Spokane only — Tri-Cities untouched, still the old model) — cap of 4 active emergencies/day per tech, no displacement as the norm.** Replaces the old "always today, push everything else later" mechanism — that was the repeated source of cascade incidents (invalid post-midnight times from several same-day emergencies each re-shifting the others).
details: **Primary path — never displaces anything:** an emergency only ever claims a genuinely open slot, checked today then the next 2 weekdays (Monday counts as a valid emergency day, same as before). If a day already has 4 emergencies, it's skipped. Queue order is oldest-first by the meld's creation date.

**12h rollover:** if an already-placed emergency isn't completed within 12 hours of its appointment's END, it's pulled back into the queue with top priority (it's now the oldest/most urgent) and re-placed for TODAY. Repeats every run until it's actually completed.

**Last-resort fallback ONLY (Florencia, 2026-07-28) — displacement is back, but bounded:** if nothing in that near-term window has real open time, the emergency is forced into the earliest weekday still under the 4/day cap by pushing non-emergency, non-manual, non-preferenced filler later that same day — same anti-cascade guards as the old mechanism (never displaces another emergency, a manual move, or a preference lock; hard ceiling at `EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE` so nothing spills into an invalid time). Prefers a day that already has the SAME property first (pairs the emergency with related work, no buffer needed, less likely to need the stretch at all) before an arbitrary day.

If a heavily-loaded tech has no room anywhere in the near term even with the forced fallback, the emergency is logged and left for the next run rather than forced somewhere invalid — a sign of a real capacity problem, not something to paper over algorithmically.
Implemented as `runEmergencyQueue()` in both `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`, replacing `insertEmergencyToday()` (removed).

rules.text: **Preference lock — honor a stated day/time/date.** If a work order's **title or chat** asks for a specific day, time, or date, the scheduler books it there and won't move it.
details: Locked jobs are exempt from compaction, blocked-day moves, and overlap moves — a stated preference is never overridden by packing.
Ordinal dates are understood ("June 18th"). A stated date of **today** books same-day; a date in the **past** is dropped (job scheduled ASAP).
Only the **title** and a genuine **chat request** count — office-hours boilerplate ("Mon–Fri 9–5") is never treated as a preference.

**Weekend/Monday exception (added 2026-07-09, extended to managers 2026-07-16):** a stated Saturday/Sunday/Monday date from the **resident, the tech, OR a manager** (e.g. a tech rescheduling around an emergency and offering to come Saturday, or a manager writing "please schedule Monday July 20th") is honored as a preference — this is the only way work lands on a reserved day. Originally resident-only, then opened to the tech's own stated day, now a manager's direct instruction counts too.

`nextOccurrenceOfDay` (both `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`) used to have a hardcoded block making "Monday" impossible to resolve as a target day even when explicitly requested — fixed 2026-07-16 so a stated Monday preference can actually be honored, not just silently dropped.

A chat-based preference normally only lives ~26h (anti-thrash — see below), which isn't enough to *permanently* protect a meld sitting on a reserved day. `hasReservedDayOverride()` in both scripts scans the **full** comment history (ignoring recency) for a resident/tech/manager message naming that specific day/date, and — without ever triggering a reschedule itself — permanently suppresses the reserved-day relocation once found. This is what makes a manager's one-time chat note as durable as a title-embedded date.

The standard "outside business hours" auto-reply text (which itself says "Monday–Friday") is explicitly excluded from all of this matching — otherwise the auto-reply's own mention of "Monday" reads as a manager stating a preference on every after-hours meld.

rules.text: **Reads the chat.** It reads each job's recent messages for reschedule requests, resident preferred times, and duration hints, and accommodates residents when possible (without overriding Emergency/Urgent).
details: A Claude "chat reader" interprets the intent; the code still applies every rule above. If it's unavailable, a keyword reader is the fallback.

**Not-yet-scheduled** jobs honor requests from the last **30 days**; **already-scheduled** jobs only act on messages from the last **~26 hours** (so an old message doesn't re-shuffle the calendar every day) — except the reserved-day override above, which is recency-exempt by design.
"Earlier / sooner / before Monday" means **avoid** that day and find an earlier slot — not book on it.
Duration hints are only trusted between **15 minutes and 4 hours** (avoids reading "within 48 hours" as a 48-hour job).

rules.text: **Append-only — the set schedule NEVER moves (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-17).** Once anything is placed it stays put: **in-house work does not move, vendor work does not move, and available dates do not move.** The scheduler only **adds** newly-created work into the **next available open slots** — it never reschedules, repacks, or pulls existing work earlier, not even for a high-priority or high-demand unit. If a unit is already scheduled late, it stays late; the way to make future units land sooner is to create/schedule the turn earlier, not to re-shuffle what's already set. Priority order (below) only sequences **new, unscheduled** work among itself — it never displaces work that's already on the calendar. (This overrides any earlier "REPACK"/priority-pull idea for pulling a late turn forward.) The **one exception** is a **cancelled move-out** (see Turns): a turn whose move-out/notice was cancelled is a *void* turn, so it's deleted outright and the slot it frees is backfilled by the next-priority unscheduled turn — that's reclaiming an invalid slot, not rescheduling valid work.
details: **Forward-compaction on early completion (added, Lee Roy 2026-07-27) — the second exception, FORWARD-ONLY.** When a turn finishes ahead of schedule, the capacity it frees IS reclaimed: `pm_compact_turns.js` (runs in each turn workflow, dedupe → **compact** → schedule → final-walk) pulls later turns' scheduled in-house work **earlier** to fill the opening. Strict guards: **only ever moves a meld to an EARLIER date** (never later); keeps each turn on its assigned tech + 2-paint→1-maint structure; still honors **LEAD_DAYS** (never today/tomorrow — the team still gets notice), Mon-Thu, and no double-booking; **never moves a STARTED/PENDING_COMPLETION/completed meld** (those anchor their days); fills in priority order (leased → Converted → Converting → days-vacant → rent). So "the set schedule never moves LATER" still holds — it may only compress forward when real capacity opens up.

rules.text: don't reshuffle without a reason — only move work for a higher priority, a past-due job, or a valid resident conflict.

any appointment that lands on a reserved day (Mon/Sat/Sun) or that double-books a tech is automatically relocated — unless it's backed by a stated preference lock (see the weekend exception above), which is left alone. **In Tacoma and Spokane this is now gated by the freeze rule below** (Tri-Cities is unaffected, still gated by manual-only).

**Manual assignment is sacred (firm rule, Florencia 2026-07-22, the MOST important rule alongside the one below) — applies in every region, no exceptions.** Once a meld has ANY assignee — a technician (even one outside that region's normal pool) OR a vendor — no scheduler ever takes it away or hands it to someone else. Only a genuinely unassigned meld (no in-house servicer, no active vendor request) is ever auto-claimed.
details: **Vendor assignments are easy to miss:** they live in the `vendor_assignment_requests` field, a SEPARATE field from `in_house_servicers`. A meld handed to a vendor still shows an *empty* `in_house_servicers` list, so any check that only looks at `in_house_servicers` sees it as "unassigned" and will silently steal it back for a technician. **Real incident (2026-07-22):** this happened in Tri-Cities — assigning a meld to a vendor got it silently un-assigned and handed back to Jared/Jaxson. Fixed the same day in all three repair schedulers (`pm_scheduler.js`, `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`, `pm_tricities_scheduler.js`) via a shared `hasActiveVendorAssignment()` check (a vendor request counts as active unless it's `rejected` or `canceled`).

Tacoma used to have a "steal it back for Jonas" branch for a meld sitting on a tech who doesn't work Tacoma (e.g. Margarito). **Removed 2026-07-22** as part of this same rule — Tacoma now only ever claims a truly unassigned meld, matching Spokane's convention (a8e392f, 2026-07-20) and Tri-Cities.

rules.text: **Manual appointment moves are sacred (firm rule, Florencia 2026-07-20, made universal 2026-07-22) — Tri-Cities.** If a person moves a meld's appointment by hand in the PropertyMeld UI, no scheduler ever touches that appointment again — not via compaction, emergency-insertion displacement, or the reserved-day/overlap self-heal. Every scheduler always logs in as the same "Ridgeview Scheduler" service account (persona id **62267**); every appointment carries an `update_by`/`create_by` persona id, so if the last touch came from a *different* persona, a human did it by hand. Implemented as `wasManuallyMoved()`, unchanged in `pm_tricities_scheduler.js`.

**Freeze — Tacoma and Spokane only (firm rule, Florencia 2026-07-28, supersedes "manual is sacred" in these two regions).** Nothing with a placed appointment moves via ANY self-heal path (reserved-day, overlap, same-day/cross-day compaction, past-due) — manual or bot-placed — until **30 hours past the appointment's END time with no completion ("30h overdue")**. Inside the **current work week (Monday–Friday)**, everything already on the calendar is frozen regardless of who placed it; outside the current week, only a genuinely manual placement (per `wasManuallyMoved()`) keeps this protection. This directly fixes a real incident (2026-07-28): the past-due check never looked at `wasManuallyMoved()` at all, so a manually-scheduled appointment (e.g. to Jacob Jett) whose date rolled into the past got silently swept up and rescheduled elsewhere the next run — that was the actual mechanism behind melds "vanishing" from a tech's calendar, separate from the stale-appointment-ordering bug fixed the same day (`2c813fa`).
details: Once something clears 30h overdue, it re-enters the normal past-due path — and that reschedule is the **one and only** case allowed to land on a **Monday** (nothing else, ever, does). Implemented via `isFrozen()` + `isOverdueHrs()` + an `allowMonday` flag on `findNextSlot`, in both `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`.
Property clustering, chat/preference actions, and emergency-today insertion are unaffected by this — see their own sections.

rules.text: always dry-run a change first. Live runs happen only in the cloud (see "How it runs").

**Repairs budget-floor list (Florencia, 2026-08-20) — Spokane and Tri-Cities repairs only (Tacoma has no flagged properties currently).** A property that ran over its AppFolio Repairs budget gets a hard floor of **2026-09-01** on any NEW or rescheduled non-emergency date — no non-emergency work is placed there before that date. This overrides every other rule in this section (freeze, compaction, past-due reshuffle, property clustering/gap-fill, daily cap, etc.) **except a manual appointment placed by a human directly in PropertyMeld** — the manual-move exemption above still applies, since the source data itself is manually verified. **Emergency/Urgent always proceeds regardless** — confirmed explicitly by Florencia, do not defer a real emergency for budget reasons.
details: Current list: **ps25, rl21** (Tri-Cities) and **k104, p705, j312, a511** (Spokane). Source of truth is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Florencia83/Reports/main/data/repairs-budget-floor.json` — built from the manually-verified "weekly update" tab of Florencia's P&L Google Sheet, **NOT** the automated `weekly-mtd.json` pipeline (that feed had known gaps as of 2026-08-20: a stale third-party QBO feed, plus CapEx/Turn purchases counted as R&M). Update that JSON file (and its `floor_date`) whenever the sheet changes — there's no automatic sync yet.

Implemented as `loadBudgetFloor()`/`applyBudgetFloor()` in `pm_spokane_scheduler.js` and `pm_tricities_scheduler.js` (each has its own copy, matching this repo's existing no-shared-lib convention for these two files) — gates `findNextSlot`/`findSlotOnDate` only, which is sufficient because the emergency path (`insertEmergencyToday`/the Spokane reserved-slot queue) never calls either function. `forceSlotOnDate` (stated-preference fallback) is deliberately NOT gated — an explicit resident/manager date preference is left alone rather than guessed about.

**Auto-releases on its own — no need to remember to edit the JSON off on Sept 1.** `applyBudgetFloor()` is a no-op once today's date reaches/passes `floor_date`, so a stale `over_budget_repairs` entry left in the file past that date has zero effect (a real reschedule attempt after the floor date can never propose an earlier date anyway, since `findNextSlot` always searches forward from today).

**Proactive move of already-scheduled work, effective 2026-08-21 ("a partir de mañana" — Florencia was explicit the change should not touch anything today, only take effect starting the next day):** a NEW step, run once at the end of each scheduler's `main()`, scans every non-emergency repair for a flagged property and — if its current appointment date is **before** the floor and **not today** — moves it to the next open slot on/after the floor, using the standard `add-management-appointment` reschedule + cancel-if-future idiom. **Today's date is explicitly excluded** ("el día de hoy queda excluido en el movimiento" — Florencia): a meld already on today's calendar is never touched, only future August dates. This is a genuine exception to the repo's append-only rule (like the cancelled-move-out and wrong-crew exceptions above) — justified the same way: reclaiming/relocating work that shouldn't be there, not arbitrary reshuffling. It overrides a stated preference lock too (per Florencia: "supera todas las reglas excepto movimiento manual" — literally every rule except a manual move), so a preference-locked meld for one of these properties dated before the floor WILL still be moved; only `wasManuallyMoved()` exempts a meld. Guarded by the same auto-release check (`today<floorDate`), so it stops running the moment the floor date passes.

Tested `DRY_RUN=1` both regions 2026-08-20 (both the gating and the proactive-move pass), ran clean — Tri-Cities moved a real RL21 meld from 08-21→09-01, Spokane moved a real one from 08-27→09-02 (09-01 is a Monday, blocked), no crashes.

rules.text: `meld created < move-in + 30 days`. Move-in comes from AppFolio `tenant_directory` (`move_in`), which is the only report carrying it for a CURRENT resident — `unit_vacancy` only covers `Vacant-*`/`Notice-*` units, so a moved-in unit is absent from it by definition.

That is exactly why they looked like misassignment during the 2026-09-02 Tri-Cities audit: 5 melds on Margarito (mailbox keys, missing appliances, inoperable fan, shower faucet, mailbox key) all sat 0–6 days past move-in.

⚠️ **The repairs scheduler must not claim them.** A warranty work order arrives unassigned like any other repair, so without an explicit carve-out the region's repair scheduler will assign it to a repair tech on its next run. A second turn tech was added 2026-08-12 and left 2026-08-19. Uses the flat 0.5h buffer throughout (no same-property zero-buffer exception like Spokane's — not needed yet, can be added if it ever matters here).

A hard-pinned title/chat date that doesn't fit with the normal buffer gets squeezed in with a tighter (or zero) buffer that day instead of running the day later — the close time never moves, even for a non-negotiable date.

rules.text: when a job needs the tenant present, the scheduler reads the tenant's chosen availability windows and books inside one.
**Pest "attend treatment" jobs** are date-pinned: the date is fixed and the exact time is vendor-driven (left to a person).
Only **one appointment per job** is kept — duplicate appointments are cleaned up so they can't cause double-booking.

**Emergency/Urgent — REWRITTEN AGAIN 2026-08-18 (Florencia), Spokane-only, overrides the general queue rule above.** The old near-term-window model (today + next 2 weekdays, no displacement as the norm, forced fallback as last resort) is replaced by a simpler reserved-capacity model, specifically to stop the calendar getting messy again: **slot 1 of every work day is reserved for a possible emergency.** Regular (non-emergency) Spokane work never starts before `REGULAR_DAY_START` (9:30am, `EMERGENCY_RESERVED_HRS`=1.5h) — so an emergency arriving on any given day almost always finds its reserved slot still open with nothing to displace. An emergency is searched for **today, then tomorrow, then the next weekday** (in order — the search skips weekends and, critically, **Mondays too**, see below), landing in the reserved slot; the old forced-displacement fallback (pushing non-emergency filler later, hard-ceilinged at `EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE`) is kept only as a genuine last-resort safety net for the rare day that already has multiple emergencies stacked. `EMERGENCY_EXTENDED_CLOSE` is now **5:00 PM** (was 6pm). Who gets an emergency is still decided by the same property-ownership rule as everything else (no automatic-to-one-tech carve-out).

**Mondays are fully blocked for Spokane repairs, NO EXCEPTIONS (Florencia, 2026-08-18) — supersedes the general "Monday is an emergency reserve" rule for this region.** Mondays must stay completely empty: not for Emergency/Urgent (the old "Monday counts as a valid emergency day" behavior is gone), and not for the 30h-overdue past-due reschedule either (the old `allowMonday` carve-out in `findNextSlot` is removed — a 30h-overdue job now waits for the next non-Monday opening like everything else). Implemented by skipping `getDay()===1` unconditionally in every Spokane day-search loop (`runEmergencyQueue`, `findNextSlot`; property clustering already skipped Monday via `isBlockedDay`).

**Daily compaction REMOVED for Spokane (Florencia, 2026-08-18).** `sameDayCompaction` (the same-day gap-closing pass that used to pull later jobs earlier to fill a hole left by a cancellation) no longer runs as part of the live daily pipeline — the calendar is not auto-reshuffled at all anymore. The only thing that still protects/moves an existing appointment is the freeze rule + "manual moves are sacred" below. (The function is kept in the file, still exported, only for the old one-time reference scripts that call it directly.)

**Daily cap — 4 non-emergency work orders per tech per day (Florencia, stated 2026-08-14, scope confirmed Spokane-repairs-only 2026-08-17).** At most `DAILY_CAP` (4) non-emergency melds get scheduled onto any one tech's day; emergencies are extra capacity on top, handled entirely by the separate emergency queue's own 4/day cap above and never counted against this one ("las emergencias son la work order extra de cada dia"). The cap is per INDIVIDUAL tech, not per team — Jacob and David are capped independently even though they share a vehicle/property. Implemented via `dayCounts`/`applyDayCap()` in `pm_spokane_scheduler.js`: a capped date gets a synthetic all-day busy block merged into that tech's search calendar, so every slot-finder rejects it the same way a reserved day would; a hard-pinned title/chat date (`forceSlotOnDate`) is the one exception, same precedent as it already overriding the normal buffer. Not yet ported to Tacoma or Tri-Cities — this was explicitly scoped to Spokane repairs only.

the 30-minute buffer between jobs exists for drive time between properties — back-to-back jobs at the SAME property (e.g. two units in the same building) need no buffer, since the team is already on site. The buffer only applies between jobs at different properties. This applies everywhere a slot is searched, including the emergency logic above.

rules.category: Property clustering (permanent, added 2026-07-01, narrowed 2026-07-09, fallback added 2026-07-28)
rules.text: plain brand-new repairs (no chat/pref/emergency trigger) are placed by building CODE PREFIX (e.g. "k104"), not pure priority+earliest-slot — the goal is the Jacob/David team spending a whole day at one property instead of bouncing around. A new job first looks for an existing future day already dedicated to its property with room; **if none, it now fills any OTHER future day that already has room (any property) before opening a fresh day** ("si no hay mas melds de esa propiedad, rellenamos con melds de otra propiedad, no importa cual" — Florencia, 2026-07-28: getting residents seen sooner outranks keeping each day one-property-only); if neither works, it starts a fresh day; if none of that is possible within 90 days, it falls back to the plain earliest-slot search so nothing goes unscheduled. Every placement here defaults to `REGULAR_DAY_START` (9:30am), not 8am — see the reserved-slot-1 rule above. 1. **Declutter:** a day where no property has 2+ melds (every job is a lone stop) has zero clustering value — relocate its singles, one at a time, to any OTHER day that already has a real cluster of its own, regardless of destination property (a lone stop's drive time doesn't depend on which day it lands on). Never dumps into another weak/lone day or a completely empty one — that would just relocate the clutter instead of solving it. Frees the day entirely for a future same-property block to move into. 2. **Gap-fill:** pulls melds forward into a day's open tail time — (a) more of that day's own property from the nearest later day, (b) a complete different-property day/group that fits the gap entirely, (c) loose singles (priority, then oldest-created first), capped to one per source day (its current last job) so a pull never leaves a fresh gap behind. 3. **Same-property consolidation:** a property scattered across multiple days is merged onto whichever of those days already has the most of it, REBUILT from 8am — that property's block first (existing + pulled-in candidates that still fit), then any other-property filler that was already on that day. **Always respects the normal 4pm close (changed 2026-07-09)** — a candidate (or the filler after it) is only pulled in if the whole day still fits by 4pm; a property with too much volume for one day simply keeps its overflow elsewhere rather than stretching the day past close. (Previously allowed running to 6pm — Florencia, 2026-07-02 — but in practice that produced non-emergency days running to 6pm and dragged unrelated filler work past close too, so it was removed.) All three passes skip today, locked/preference melds, Emergency/Urgent, and — per Florencia, originally 2026-07-02, made a rolling window 2026-07-09 — **anything within the next 14 days of whenever it's run** (`FREEZE_WINDOW_DAYS` in `pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js`); the schedule-change window only covers dates beyond that 2-week horizon, so near-term work stays stable and the cutoff never goes stale between runs. Kept manual deliberately until it's been watched working correctly for a while — it moves already-scheduled jobs across dates, which is exactly what the "never move an already-scheduled date" rule above normally forbids.
details: **Unit-level match (added 2026-08-06):** the day-matching check also fires on the more specific EXACT unit (`m.unit.id`), not just the property code — checked in the same chronological pass as the property match, so whichever qualifying day comes soonest wins regardless of which one matched ("va para el que esta primero" — Florencia, 2026-08-06).

**Adjacent placement, not just same-day (added 2026-08-07):** matching a day used to only guarantee the same DATE — `findSlotOnDate` would take the first open slot from 8am regardless of where the matching property/unit's own appointment actually sat, which could leave hours of dead time between two visits to the same address (found 2026-08-07: a same-unit follow-up landed 11am-12:30 while the existing visit for that unit was 3:30-5:30pm, same tech, same day). `findAdjacentSlot` now tries landing immediately before or after the matching appointment (zero buffer, same as the existing same-property buffer rule) first, only falling back to the old any-open-slot search if no adjacent slot fits.

**Past-due work does NOT cluster (2026-07-09):** a past-due job already carries a resident expectation from a prior date that fell through (e.g. the tech couldn't make it) — waiting for a "clean" property day to open up pushed these weeks out in practice (a real case landed a month away). Past-due jobs now take the nearest available slot on any day instead, same as a chat-driven reschedule — it can break that day's property theme for that one visit.

**Never moves the DATE of an already-scheduled job.** Same-day gap-closing (`sameDayCompaction`) used to be the one exception (sweeping each day for a cancellation-left hole and pulling later jobs earlier to close it) — **removed entirely 2026-08-18** (Florencia: stop auto-reshuffling the calendar). Nothing now moves an already-placed appointment except the reserved-day/overlap self-heal, itself gated by the freeze rule (see General).
Chat-driven reschedules and preference locks are unaffected by clustering — they keep their existing (higher-priority) behavior and can break a day's property theme for that one visit.
One-time backlog rebuild done 2026-07-01 via `pm_spokane_property_test.js` (kept in the repo as the reference implementation / for any future one-time re-clustering; not run automatically).

**One-time Jacob consolidation (2026-07-28), `pm_spokane_jacob_consolidate_onetime.js`.** Run once, before the freeze rule locked already-scheduled work in place, to pull Jacob's future backlog (scattered as far out as September) into the earliest real openings — mixing properties freely, since the goal was getting residents seen sooner, not property purity for its own sake. Skips today, reserved days, manual moves, and preference-locked melds; only ever moves a meld earlier. Kept in the repo as a reference/rerun tool, not wired to any workflow.

**Cross-day gap-filling (`pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js`, added 2026-07-02) — MANUAL only, not in any workflow.** A day that isn't fully booked 8am-4pm — including a completely empty workday sitting before later work — delays the backlog and eats an extra calendar day for no reason. Run this by hand (`DRY_RUN=1 node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` to preview, `node pm_spokane_fill_gaps.js` live). Three passes, in order:

rules.text: **David Sanchez and Alexander Overall** handle recurring "Lawn service" melds in Spokane (plus Our Natural Homes). Repairs and other techs' work are not touched.
Each week's recurring lawn melds are snapped to a **canonical template week** (a fixed day, time, and duration per property) and mirrored forward **+7 days**, so the times never drift week to week.
details: A property lands on the calendar as often as PropertyMeld generates its instance — most are weekly; a few (e.g. h731) are intentionally bi-weekly.

**h731 duplicate recurrence removed (2026-07-16):** h731 briefly had two PropertyMeld recurrences pointing at the same slot — one correct (every 15 days, id 163904) and one duplicate firing every 7 days (id 179920). Florencia deleted the 7-day one in PropertyMeld; the TEMPLATE in `pm_lawn_scheduler.js` now only maps the bi-weekly id.

**o155-Elm added to the template (2026-07-16, id 162926):** a separate recurrence from o155-Oak (162927) that had been running unscheduled/manual. Now fixed to Thursday 12:30 PM (1.25h), right after o155-Oak's slot ends.

**c702 "Dumpster Pick Up" added to the template (2026-08-11, id 186065):** Friday 12:15 PM (1h), right after k308. First non-"Lawn service"-titled recurring meld on this route, so the scope filter (which only matched `brief_description` against "Lawn service") had to widen to also admit any `recurring_meld` id already whitelisted in TEMPLATE — otherwise a correctly templated meld with a different title is silently dropped before the TEMPLATE lookup ever runs.
A new recurrence not yet in the template is flagged as UNKNOWN so it can be added to the template.

rules.text: **Chad Cariquist** (started 2026-08-24, replacing Taylor Perez, who replaced Reynaldo Leonides "Rey", fired 2026-08-17) handles lawn, city-clustered: Mon+Tue kn47-K1 (two weekly blocks), Wed kn47-K1 "extras" (periodic items — bed weeding, irrigation checks, tree limb clearance, flower bed refresh, weed spraying — each has its own fixed Wednesday slot so simultaneous due-dates never overlap), Thu Richland (rl16 + rl21), Fri Pasco (ps17 + ps25 + ps91). Each swap in this seat keeps the exact same template — no change to the split itself, just a name swap (`CHAD_TEMPLATE`, née `TAYLOR_TEMPLATE`, née `REY_TEMPLATE`, in `pm_tricities_grounds_scheduler.js`).
**Hannah Deckard** handles grounds/porter work: Tue Pasco, Wed Richland, Mon/Thu/Fri Kennewick (kn47 K1).

**Scope is deliberately narrow — recurring melds ONLY.** One-off melds for Rey/Hannah (sprinkler repairs, pest issues, bulk furniture, etc.) are always placed manually by Florencia or the tech — this scheduler never touches them, and has no Emergency/Urgent override logic (not needed since one-offs, where an emergency would live, are out of scope entirely).
**No Monday reserve** — unlike Tacoma/Spokane, Chad and Hannah work a normal Mon–Fri week (no emergency-driven Monday hold), same as Spokane's David/Alexander.
**Never touches the current week** — only schedules starting the Monday after the current week, same convention as the Spokane lawn template.

runs every 3 days, so it doesn't map to one fixed weekday like the rest of the template. It rotates through a fixed 3-slot cycle each time a new instance needs placing — Mon 06:00 → Wed 06:00 → Fri 10:15 → back to Mon — rather than a single fixed day. Hannah moves it by hand if the auto-picked day doesn't match actual need.

when a resident gives notice or moves out, AppFolio sets a move-out date and a **Standard Unit Turn** project is created in PropertyMeld for that unit. The turn's start date is the **day after the move-out date**. One turn per unit — duplicates are skipped.
**Techs — per region.** In-house turn work is always **paint and maintenance only**; cleaning and flooring are vendors everywhere.
details: **Spokane:** Ron Cramer and Micheal Magoon for everything except c702 (Matt Romme + Brady Smith). Scott Higley no longer works here; **Justin Gutierrez was terminated 2026-09-02** after three weeks on the crew. Ron and Magoon are the **only** general-crew turn techs — no additional Spokane hires (an earlier note claimed two more start July 20, 2026; that hire never happened — corrected 2026-07-17).

**Tri-Cities (updated 2026-09-02, Lee Roy):** **Matthew Williams (63593, started 2026-08-24)** + **Danny Halfacre (63873, started 2026-09-02)** do paint/maint, **split evenly** between them. **Margarito Saldana (48464) does the walkthroughs** — every initial walkthrough and final QC — **plus up to 2 days of turn work per week** ("Margarito can work on turns for 2 days per week"). Three turn team members, no others. James Dunlap and Ryan Robson left 2026-08-24.

This ends the 2026-08-24 stopgap that had Margarito on **full-time** paint/maint (4 days most weeks) because James and Ryan had gone and Matthew was the only turn tech. Walkthroughs are his job again; turn work is the capacity he absorbs around them.
**The 2-day cap is `WEEK_CAP` in `pm_tricities_turn_scheduler.js`** (env `MARG_TURN_DAYS_PER_WEEK`). Two things about it are load-bearing:

⛔ **It must be checked CUMULATIVELY across the days being placed, not one day at a time.** Paint is 2 consecutive days; testing each against a count not yet updated sees "1 used, cap 2" twice and books both, landing him on 3. `canTakeDays()` sums the whole request per ISO week before agreeing to any of it.

⛔ **A capped tech is a FALLBACK, not a peer.** The tech-selection tie-break prefers whoever has fewer booked days — and a capped tech always has fewer, so left alone he wins every tie and absorbs the rota he is meant to be a relief valve for. `beats()` prefers an uncapped tech on an equal start day; Margarito only wins by being strictly earlier.
"Evenly" between Matthew and Danny needs no special algorithm: earliest start wins, lighter calendar breaks the tie, which self-balances across two techs.

⚠️ `occ` must cover the walk tech too, not just `TURN_TECHS`. `walkSlot()` reads `occ[WALK_TECH.id]` to cap a day he is already booked on down to a single 1-hour overlay; leaving it undefined makes the cap `SLOTS.length` and the scheduler stacks up to seven walkthroughs onto a day he is out painting.
**Backlog handed over 2026-09-02** — see the one-time `pm_tricities_role_split.js` note below.

**Tacoma:** **Chris Phillips paints, Armani Mitchell maintains and does every walkthrough** (split roles, 2026-08-19). See the Tacoma section for the 2-paint-**2**-maint exception; QC is always Armani, own units included.

rules.text: **Tri-Cities backlog handover, 2026-09-02 — `pm_tricities_role_split.js` (one-time, applied).** Adding Danny changed nothing on its own: all 41 open Tri-Cities turns were already booked (Matthew 52 days to 12-01, Margarito 48 to 11-24, Danny 0), and gap-fill only touches melds with no appointment. **35 melds across 18 turns were reassigned**, trimming Margarito to his 2-day-a-week cap and splitting the rest evenly — final: Matthew 40 days, Danny 41, Margarito 24.
details: 🔑 **This was the SAFE class of rebalance because NO DATE MOVED.** Danny's calendar was empty, so every date was already free on him: it is a change of *who*, never of *when*. Nothing downstream (QC chain, AppFolio availability) needed recomputing, no available date could move OUT, and the append-only rule was never even engaged — no appointment was created or cancelled, only `in_house_servicers` changed. That also makes it genuinely reversible, which a date change would not be (cancelled PM appointments cannot be read back). Snapshot at `C:/Users/lrphi/tricities_rebalance_snapshot.json`; `node pm_tricities_role_split.js revert apply` puts every meld back.

🔑 **The movable unit is the TURN, not the meld or the day.** A unit's paint and maintenance must stay on one tech, so moving melds individually would silently break that rule. Verified after the write: no double-bookings, no unit split across techs, 0 dates changed, 35/35 confirmed by independent read-back.

⚠️ **3 turns could not be placed without moving dates** (kn47 K1 #A103, rl16 #C20, ps25 #D29) and were left alone, so Margarito is still over his 2-day cap in 3 weeks (W36, W43, W45). Correcting those needs date moves and therefore separate authorisation — it was not done silently.

rules.text: **When a region GAINS a tech, the backlog does not move on its own — check it (learned twice, 2026-08-12).** Gap-fill only schedules melds with **no appointment**, so where every open turn is already placed the new tech gets **nothing** and sits idle behind the queue (Tacoma: 25 turns all on Armani to 2027-02-02 when a second tech arrived; Spokane: 65 turns all on Ron + Magoon to 2026-12-02 when Justin moved over, him 0). Redistributing means moving placed work, so it needs an explicit authorisation — the tool is `turn_rebalance_plan.js` (read-only, `REGION=tacoma|spokane`) then `turn_rebalance_apply.js`.
details: 🔑 **GAIN-ONLY is the default and the reason it is safe.** A unit's re-placement is kept **only if that unit finishes strictly earlier**; otherwise it is rolled back and the unit keeps exactly what it had. Without it a full re-pack only helps a backlog *concentrated* on too few techs: on an already-distributed, densely-packed schedule it reshuffles instead of improving (Spokane's first pass pushed **28** vacant units later for a 13-day tail gain; a Tacoma re-run pushed **13** later). Both were refused by the forward-only check — but refusing is not the same as doing the useful subset.

⚠️ **When a placement is rolled back, its ORIGINAL days must be re-blocked.** They were freed during seeding on the assumption the unit would move; keeping the unit means those days are occupied again. Missing this put `c702 #A201` straight on top of the rolled-back `a210 #8`'s 09-02/09-03/09-07 on Magoon — caught by the apply pre-flight.

⚠️ **The apply script re-checks forward-only itself.** The planner refuses to *recommend* a regressive plan but still leaves the plan file on disk, which a careless apply would use. Enforce the ceiling twice.

⚠️ **Only a conflict the write CAUSES is fatal.** Pre-existing clashes between appointments already on the calendar (e.g. two short repairs in one hour on a repairs tech) are reported, not blocking — otherwise the check can never pass on a messy calendar.

rules.text: **2 back-to-back days of paint, then 1 day of maintenance**, all done by the **same tech** (one tech per unit). Plus a **1-hour initial walkthrough** the day after the unit vacates, split between both techs.

**Monday–Thursday, 8 AM–4 PM. Friday is left open** as a buffer for delays; no weekend work. A turn's paint→maintenance may bridge the Friday/weekend (e.g. paint Thursday + Monday). Both techs are kept fully booked Mon–Thu to finish turns as fast as possible.

**NEVER schedule in-house work on or before the move-out date — AppFolio is the authority, NOT PropertyMeld's project start_date (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-08-12).** A turn's in-house work can only start the **day after the resident actually leaves**. PropertyMeld's project `start_date` is stamped when the turn is **created** and is **never updated if the move-out is later rescheduled**, so it silently goes stale and cannot be used as the floor.
details: Real incident (2026-08-12): **tc68 #A06**'s notice moved out to **2026-08-27** while PM still said `start_date` 2026-07-28. A rebalance floored on `start_date` therefore booked paint for **08-17** — on an apartment the resident was still living in. Caught by an audit comparing every unit's first in-house day against its AppFolio `last_move_out`; it was the only unit affected, and the work was moved to 11-09.

`last_move_out` in the `unit_vacancy` report holds the **scheduled future** move-out for a `Notice-*` unit, so it is the right field for both vacant and on-notice units. Floor every unit at `max(LEAD_DAYS, project start, move-out + 1)`.

**A unit that is still occupied AND booked too early goes to the BACK of the queue** — it can't be worked yet, and an unleased future vacancy is the lowest priority tier anyway. But a not-yet-vacant unit whose work is **already validly placed after its move-out keeps its slot**: pushing valid work later would breach the never-move-work-out rule for no reason (tc68 #B60, move-out 09-01 with work from 09-23, was briefly shoved 37 days out by a blanket version of this rule — don't reintroduce that).
Implemented in `pm_tacoma_turn_scheduler.js` + the rebalance planner. ⚠️ **Spokane and Tri-Cities do NOT have this floor yet** — they still trust `start_date`. Worth adding.

rules.text: **Vendor work sitting on a tech's calendar is VISIBILITY ONLY and must never block his own work (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-08-12).** Armani puts the vendor stages (**F - Cleaning**, **E - Carpet Cleaning**) on his own calendar so he can see the whole turn pipeline — *"he only puts vendor work on his calendar for visibility, it's not a task he's actually doing"*. Treating those as all-day blocks costs real capacity for work no tech performs: it was holding roughly **11 days** of Tacoma turn schedule hostage and skewing the two-tech split.
details: So when building a tech's busy days, **skip cleaning and carpet melds** even when he is an `in_house_servicer` on them. Test carpet first so "E - Carpet Cleaning" reads as carpet rather than cleaning.
The **final walkthrough is NOT vendor work** — a tech really does that QC, so it still occupies his calendar (as a short appointment).
This is separate from the older lesson that busy blocks must cover a tech's **entire** calendar: they still must, but a visibility-only vendor meld is not really his work in the first place.

rules.text: **Lead time — a few days' notice, never today/tomorrow (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-27).** Newly-scheduled turn work (initial walkthrough, paint, maintenance, and the final QC walkthrough) is placed no sooner than **3 days out** (`LEAD_DAYS`, env-overridable in every turn scheduler + both final-walkthrough scripts) so the team always has a few days to adapt — the automation never books work on today or tomorrow. Already-scheduled work is untouched (append-only).

applies **only to new, unscheduled turns** as they're added — it never re-orders or pulls forward turns already on the calendar (see the append-only rule in "General"). New turns are sequenced by a strict priority ladder: **(1) leased units first** (a new tenant is already lined up, so the move-in deadline is firm), by soonest move-in date; then **(2) units with a Converted application**, by earliest desired move-in date; then **(3) units with a Converting application**, by earliest desired move-in date; then **(4) most days vacant** (longest-vacant unit first, to clear the oldest vacancies fastest); then **(5) highest scheduled rent**. Only **Converted** and **Converting** applications count toward the desired-move-in tiers — **Converted always outranks Converting** — because those are the prospects actually likely to sign; every other application status is ignored for scheduling priority.
who does it, per region (rewritten 2026-08-12, Lee Roy).
details: **Spokane: a TURN TECH does the QC, but NEVER the tech who turned the unit.** *"if michael turns the unit, ron will do the walkthrough. if matt turns the unit brady will do the walkthrough or vise versa."* Pairs: **Magoon ↔ Ron**, **Matt Romme ↔ Brady Smith**. Justin Gutierrez has no fixed partner yet, so he falls back to "any turn tech who didn't work on it". This **retires David Sanchez from turn QC** — he keeps grounds/lawn. If every configured tech worked a unit, the run logs it rather than allowing self-QC.

**Tacoma: Armani does ALL walkthroughs, including on units he turned himself.** *"in tacoma, armani does all the walkthroughs even if he turned the unit."* A deliberate exception — do not "fix" this toward independence. (Earlier the same day it was changed to split QC across two techs on the assumption independence was wanted; that was reversed.)
**Tri-Cities:** Margarito Saldana does walkthroughs only (no paint/maint), so it is independent by construction.

rules.text: **A QC IS NEVER BOOKED AFTER THE TENANT MOVES IN — the move-in beats LEAD_DAYS (added 2026-08-12).** The 3-day lead-time floor exists to give the team notice; a committed move-in is a harder constraint, so where they conflict the floor yields and the QC is pulled in front of the move-in.
details: This was a real silent regression: **c313 #33, w117 #3 and c302 #5** all had their make-ready work finished but their QC sitting *after* the tenant's move-in. They were corrected by hand, and the very next scheduler run would have pushed them straight back — the script recomputes the date from the vendor chain and had no notion of a move-in.

⚠️ **The pull-in only applies if the WORK is already finished by the earlier date.** Signing off before the work exists is meaningless: a naive version of this clamp yanked `k104 #101-1` (paint 09-17, maint 09-22) back to 08-13. When the *work* is what's late, moving the QC cannot fix it — the run surfaces it as **"work finishes after the tenant moves in"** for a person to reschedule or to tell the tenant.

rules.category: SPOKANE HAS TWO SEPARATE TURN CREWS
rules.text: NOT INTERCHANGEABLE (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-08-13).
details: **c702 → Matt Romme (63325) + Brady Smith (63324), EXCLUSIVELY.** They were onboarded for the 19 c702 turns and hold only c702 work; c702 is their whole scope. **Empty weekdays on their calendars once the current c702 turns are done are EXPECTED, not a scheduling fault.**
**Everything else in Spokane → Ron + Magoon + Justin, EXCLUSIVELY.**
This mirrors the cleaning split (c702 = U&K, rest = SPO Cleaning) and the QC pairing (Matt ↔ Brady, Magoon ↔ Ron).

⚠️ **HOW THIS BROKE: a rebalance that does not list every tech will STRIP the ones it cannot see.** On 2026-08-12 the Spokane rebalance listed only Ron/Magoon/Justin, read Matt's and Brady's days as free, and moved **10 c702 units off them** — leaving two techs with empty weekdays from late August. **Any tool that reassigns turns must list EVERY tech (so their calendars are respected) AND enforce the crew split.** Fixed in `pm_spokane_turn_scheduler.js` (`crewFor()`) and `turn_rebalance_plan.js` (a `crews` config plus `wrongCrew` detection).

**Work on the wrong crew MUST move even if it lands later** — the correct crew is smaller, so returning c702 to two people cost 2–9 days per unit. That is the accepted price of correct assignment, and it is exempt from the forward-only ceiling (like a move-out violation).

rules.text: **CLEANING IS AUTOMATED FOR SPOKANE (added 2026-08-13, Lee Roy).** `pm_spokane_cleaning.js`, step 5 of the Spokane turn workflow — it runs **before** the final walkthrough on purpose, because the QC date is derived from the last vendor task.
details: **Who gets it:** every Spokane property **except c702** → **SPO Cleaning** (id `97680`, `sierrazinnerman@spocleaningmaids.com` — this *is* "Spo Cleaning Maids"; the PropertyMeld record is just named "SPO Cleaning"). **c702** → **U&K Properties LLC** (id `77472`).

**⛔ Carpet cleaning is NOT scheduled** — "E - Carpet Cleaning" melds are left alone entirely. Carpet is tested *first* in the matcher so "E - Carpet Cleaning" can never be mistaken for the cleaning meld.
**Requested date = last in-house day + 3 business days**, floored at the next business day — the same rule the final-walkthrough scheduler uses, so cleaning and QC stay consistent.

🔑 **VENDOR ASSIGNMENT *IS* AVAILABLE BY API — the old note saying it wasn't is wrong.** `PATCH /api/melds/{id}/assign-maintenance/` with `{ maintenance: [{ id: <vendorId>, type: 'Vendor' }], user_groups: [] }`. The endpoint is generic; `type` discriminates a vendor from an in-house tech. It creates the `vendor_assignment_request`, moves the meld to `PENDING_VENDOR`, notifies the vendor, and sets `accept_by` ~4 days out.

⚠️ **BUT WE CANNOT SET THE VENDOR'S DATE — the vendor books it.** `assignments/{id}/segments/` returns 400 before acceptance ("Can't update an assignment that hasn't been accepted") and 500 after; `vendor-appointments/{id}/schedule/` 500s on every payload shape; PATCH on the appointment is 405. Decisive evidence: **every pre-existing cleaning appointment was created by the vendor's persona (`org_type: "v"`)**, never by management. So the requested date is sent as a **vendor-visible comment** (`hidden_from_vendor: false`, `response_required: true`) carrying an `[auto-cleaning]` marker for idempotency, and the vendor confirms.

⛔ **THE SCRIPT NO LONGER TRIES TO BOOK THE VENDOR'S DATE (removed 2026-08-15).** "Stage B" used to PUT `/api/assignments/{id}/segments/` once a vendor accepted. Given the line above, that could never succeed — and it didn't: **"0 booked" in every run since it shipped**, re-firing a guaranteed 500 on the same units every morning (`e328 #5` from 08-14, `p705 #19` from 08-15) and logging them as `failed`. The file had *documented* the impossibility and then attempted the write anyway, rationalised as "fails softly; if PropertyMeld ever accepts a management-set segment it will start working." **A documented impossibility must not be retried daily on the chance the vendor's platform changed** — that is how a known limitation turns into permanent log noise that masks real failures.

Accepted-but-unbooked is now **reported, not retried**: `awaiting vendor booking` in the summary, listed under "ACCEPTED BUT NOT BOOKED — needs a nudge from a person." Nothing in the automation can move it forward, so a human chases the vendor.

Deliberately **no second nudge comment** — the `[auto-cleaning]` request already gave them the date and asked them to confirm; another automated message would just re-create the vendor spam removed the same day.

`putSegments()` and the `CLEAN_START`/`CLEAN_END` appointment-time settings were **deleted**, not left dormant: the time was never ours to choose, and dead code encoding a false belief invites someone to "fix the payload" on a call that cannot work.

⛔ **`/api/comments/` RETURNS A BARE ARRAY, NOT `{results:[...]}` — this broke idempotency (Lee Roy, 2026-08-15: *"the turn scheduler sends a message to the vendor everyday, this should only happen once"*).** `pm_spokane_cleaning.js` read `JSON.parse(body).results || []`; `.results` on an array is `undefined`, the fallback made it an **empty list**, so the `[auto-cleaning]` marker was never found and the date request was re-sent on **every daily run** — **20 c702 units were re-messaged on 08-14 and again on 08-15**. `pm_scheduler.js` and `pm_spokane_scheduler.js` had always normalised both shapes (`if (!Array.isArray(x)) x = x.results || []`); the newer script didn't. **Any new code reading comments must handle both shapes.** Note the melds/projects endpoints DO return `{results, next}` — it is specifically comments that differ, which is exactly why the mistake is easy to make.

The check now returns **true / false / null**, and a `null` (unreadable thread) **HOLDS instead of posting** — same principle as the Rent Ready rule: a check that cannot find evidence must hold, never proceed. A duplicate message to a vendor is a real-world cost, so silence beats a guess.
The **STAGE A** path (no active vendor request → assign + request) had **no marker check at all**, so a lapsed/rejected request would re-send too. Both send paths are guarded now.

⚠️ **`POST /api/add-new-vendor-appointment/meld/{id}/` returns 201 but persists only an EMPTY placeholder appointment** — a misleading success that leaves the meld stuck in `PENDING_MORE_VENDOR_AVAILABILITY`. Don't use it.

**Append-only:** a cleaning meld that already has a vendor appointment is never touched; an existing assignment is never duplicated. Safe to re-run daily, which also re-assigns anything whose ~4-day accept window lapsed.

rules.category: Vendors (coming once the new techs start)
rules.text: cleaning (Spo Cleaning) is scheduled after paint and maintenance finish, with a **2-business-day buffer** (maintenance Monday → cleaning Thursday); carpet cleaning (Allklean) the day after cleaning; flooring/carpet replacement by Inland Pacific Flooring; the final walkthrough the day after carpet cleaning.
once the work is scheduled, the unit's **Available date and Ready-to-Show date are set to the same day**, and **Rent Ready is set to "No."**
details: **Rent Ready is now set in BOTH directions, on verified evidence only (changed 2026-08-04, Lee Roy).** This supersedes the old "only the turn manager sets Yes — the automation never does" rule, which left finished turns sitting at No until a person noticed: ps25 #F43, rl16 #A04 and ps17 #A3 were all found that way, up to five weeks after their turns completed. The automation may now set **Yes** when a turn is **verified complete** — a final walkthrough COMPLETED after the move-out — and **No** when it can prove the unit was not turned since the move-out. The evidence bar is identical in both directions, and **no evidence means no change** in either. Manual overrides still win: `pm_avail_plan_manual.json` beats any builder row for the same unit. The available date is **3 days after the final walkthrough** (a buffer for punch-list items found at the walkthrough or vendor delays); until the vendor steps are automated, it's an interim **7 days after maintenance is completed**.

⚠️ **A LEASED UNIT IS NEVER "AVAILABLE" AFTER ITS TENANT ARRIVES — cap the date at the move-in (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-08-12: *"why are their available dates for after the move in date???"*).** The **+3** in *final walkthrough + 3* is a punch-list / vendor-slip buffer for **marketing a vacant unit**. Applied blindly to a unit that is **already leased**, it advertises the unit as unavailable on a day somebody is moving in — a contradiction that was live on **5 units** (c313 #33 7d after, w117 #3 6d, s129 #9 7d, e328 #4 3d, k104 #101-1 1d).
So: `available_on = min(final walk + 3, next_move_in)`. Capping is always a move **CLOSER**, so the ratchet permits it with no authorisation.
**Hitting the cap is itself a signal** — it means the turn has **zero slack** before the tenant arrives, so the runs report a `capped at move-in` count rather than swallowing it.
Fixed in `pm_avail_plan.js`, `pm_avail_plan_tc.js`, `pm_avail_plan_tac.js` and `af_portfolio_plan.js` — at the source, so the daily run cannot reintroduce it.

**Available dates only move CLOSER, never OUT (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-27).** An available date may be moved **earlier** (closer) whenever the turn will finish sooner, but is **never** pushed **later** (out) — for ANY unit. This is absolute for a **leased / Converted / Converting** unit, whose date is a commitment to a prospect: never move it out under any circumstance. (This is the standing ratchet, stated as a hard rule — the avail-write step must ratchet each date down-only and skip any write that would move a date later.)

**Don't churn small pull-ins (Lee Roy 2026-07-27):** only bother pulling an available date **closer** when it's more than **~2 weeks (14 days, `AVAIL_PULL_THRESHOLD`)** beyond the new projection; a smaller improvement is left as-is. (Implemented in `pm_avail_plan.js` + `pm_avail_plan_tc.js`.)

rules.text: **Rent Ready "Yes" must be DISPROVED before it is flipped to "No" (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-29).** A vacant unit showing Rent Ready = Yes is ambiguous: it can be stale data on a unit that was never turned, or it can be perfectly correct because the unit really was turned after the resident left. The bright line is **a final walkthrough that COMPLETED after the unit's move-out date**. Final walk completed after the move-out → the unit was genuinely turned, **keep Yes**. A final walk completed but the move-out date is unknown → **hold** (it can't be proven either way, so don't touch it). No completed final walk at all → safe to set No. A check that cannot find evidence must **hold, not proceed** — absence of data is never grounds for a destructive change.
details: **Every VACATED unit is checked, not just the ones with turn work already scheduled (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-08-03).** The riskiest unit is the one that just went vacant with **no turn scheduled at all** — it has no projected available date, and for months that meant it was filtered out before the Rent Ready check ever ran. That is exactly how **tc68 #D096** sat advertised as Rent Ready with a 7/30 move-out and no turn project in PropertyMeld. Only the **date** write depends on having a projection; the Rent Ready check never does.

**Read turn completion from PropertyMeld directly, across OPEN and CLOSED projects.** A fully-turned unit's project is **closed**, so it is absent from the turns report feed — and reading completion from that feed makes a genuinely-turned unit look never-turned. (On 2026-08-03 this would have wrongly flipped 6 Tacoma units: tc34 #A106, tc68 #C64/#C65/#C67/#D080/#D094.) Always go to the source, and include closed projects.

⚠️ **`pm_avail_plan_manual.json` IS APPLY-ONCE-THEN-DELETE, and a stale row silently undoes correct work (2026-08-12).** A manual row beats any builder row for the same unit, so a row left behind after its situation changed keeps forcing an obsolete date forever — and because the write "succeeds" and verifies against its own stale target, it reports ✅. `af_run.js` says so in a comment ("the file is not auto-generated; delete it once applied") but nothing enforces it.

Real incident: 19 rows written 2026-08-06 for the **single-tech Tacoma de-collide** schedule survived two full reschedules (a tech rebalance + a final-walkthrough refresh). On the next `af_run.js all` they **suppressed 11 Tacoma pull-ins** (e.g. tc68 #D088 forced to 11-01 when the real projection was 09-27) and **reverted tc68 #A02 from an authorised 08-20 push-out back to 08-13** — leaving it advertised *earlier* than it can actually be ready, which the ratchet then makes permanent.

Rules: **prune a manual row the moment its basis changes**; a row whose `why` cites a schedule that no longer exists is obsolete by construction. Before any `af_run.js` run, diff the manual file against the fresh builder output and question every collision. Keep only rows encoding **evidence the builders cannot derive** (turn verified complete, melds cancelled instead of completed, a pest-date correction) — never rows that merely restate a schedule, because schedules move.

**A Rent-Ready-only correction must not disturb the available date.** When a unit needs Rent Ready = No but has no new projected date, write its **existing** date straight back unchanged so the ratchet is untouched. If it has no date at all, there is **no safe automated write** — surface it for a person instead of writing a blank.

rules.text: **"Pest Control" projects are NOT turns — never let them drive turn dates (Lee Roy 2026-08-04).** The PropertyMeld projects endpoint's `project_type=TURN` filter is **not strict**: Pest Control projects (type `OTHER`) come back too, and their melds are lettered exactly like turn melds ("D - 1st Treatment", "F - 2nd Treatment"), so a category matcher reads them as maintenance and cleaning. That produced real published dates: rl21 #9 and #11 both advertised **2026-07-08** off a pest treatment while their actual turns finish 08-17 and 09-30. Always filter turn projects by **name** — `/turn/i.test(name) && !/pest/i.test(name)` — the same idiom `pm_dedupe_turns.js` and `pm_compact_turns.js` already use. Pest work also runs on **occupied** units, so it must never be treated as a turn anywhere.
details: **A bogus EARLY date is not self-correcting.** The ratchet only moves dates closer, so once a too-early date is written it sticks until a human authorises a push-out. That makes date *sources* worth guarding carefully — a wrong early date is more expensive than a missing one.

rules.text: **A unit that moved out with NO turn project at all is a defect to surface (Lee Roy 2026-08-03).** Detection/creation can miss a unit, and the failure is silent — the unit simply sits vacant with no work planned, sometimes still advertised as rent-ready. This is tracked separately from a wrong Rent Ready flag because it needs a turn **created**, not a status corrected. Standing audit: `rr_audit.js` (read-only, all regions) reports both classes — (A) Rent Ready = Yes but not turned since the move-out, (B) moved out but no turn project exists.

**Carpet: cleaning is automated, REPLACEMENT is not — a person handles it (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-30).** The standard turn template creates an **E - Carpet Cleaning** meld and nothing else carpet-related; carpet **replacement** is never auto-created, auto-scheduled, or auto-suggested. Do not build automation for it. (Confirmed 2026-07-30: the turn template creates 8 melds — walkthrough, paint, maintenance, cleaning, carpet cleaning, lockbox check, estimate, final walkthrough — and the turn schedulers only place in-house paint/maintenance/walkthrough, so replacement is untouched today. Keep it that way.)
details: **A cancelled or removed E-Carpet meld is a SIGNAL, not missing data (Lee Roy 2026-07-30):** it means either the unit has no carpet, or **the carpet is being replaced and a person will create that meld**. Either way there is nothing to carpet-clean — so the report must **not** emit a suggested carpet-cleaning date, and the final walkthrough is timed off **cleaning** instead. A vendor suggestion is only ever emitted when a meld actually exists, is not cancelled, and is not completed — never merely because no appointment is booked. (Fixed 2026-07-30 in `reports/scripts/fetch-data.js` — the copy the cloud runs every 15 min — and its local twin `pm-turn-dashboard-gen.js`. It had been emitting 32 phantom carpet visits out of 89, 22 of them at rl21.)

rules.text: **Cancelled move-out / notice-to-vacate → delete the turn (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-17).** If a unit's move-out or notice-to-vacate is cancelled (the resident is staying), that unit is no longer turning: the turn is **unscheduled** (all its PropertyMeld appointments cancelled) and the **turn project is removed completely** (its open melds and the project deleted). This frees the days it was holding on Ron/Magoon's calendars, and the next daily gap-fill run **fills that opening with the next-highest-priority unscheduled turn** (per the priority ladder above). This is the only case where already-scheduled in-house work is removed — it isn't a reschedule of valid work, it's reclaiming a slot for a turn that shouldn't exist anymore (so it stays consistent with the append-only rule).

**Move-out changes — checked daily by `af_moveout_watch.js` (built 2026-08-12, Lee Roy asked for it explicitly).** AppFolio is compared against every open turn each day, looking for move-out dates that **changed** and for units that **dropped off the vacancy report because the resident never left**. A cancelled move-out triggers the delete-the-turn rule above; a changed move-out date shifts the turn's start (new work is added per the append-only rule — existing placed work is not moved), and work that would now land on an occupied unit must be pushed past the move-out. 1. in-house work scheduled **on/before** a unit's move-out (the hard violation); 2. PropertyMeld `start_date` **earlier** than move-out + 1 — meaning the move-out was pushed back after the turn was created and PM never followed. **Direction matters:** *earlier* is the dangerous A06 pattern, while *later* just means the turn was created after the resident had already gone (harmless, ~55 units, summarised not listed). And an early start_date is only **live risk while the move-out is still in the future** — once the resident has gone the LEAD_DAYS floor covers it. Filtering that way cut the noise from 66 rows to 2 real ones; a daily check that lists 66 benign rows is a daily check nobody reads. 3. an open turn whose unit is **absent from `unit_vacancy` entirely** — that report only ever returns `Vacant-*` / `Notice-*` units, so disappearing *is* the "they didn't move out" signal. A turn with completed work is flagged for human review rather than deletion (same carve-out `pm_cancelled_turn_cleanup.js` makes).
details: ⚠️ **This bullet used to claim the daily check existed when it did not.** Only the *cancellation* half was ever implemented (`pm_cancelled_turn_cleanup.js`); nothing watched a move-out **date** move. That is precisely how tc68 #A06 slipped through. Don't let the rulebook describe intentions as if they were code.

It runs as **step 2 of `C:/Users/lrphi/af_daily.cmd`** (the local daily AppFolio run — it needs AppFolio, which has no write API and no cloud-friendly login). It is **read-only**: it reports and it remembers, never reschedules or deletes. It **always exits 0** so findings can't abort the availability write behind it.
What it checks — three **stateless** invariants that fire correctly even on a first run, plus a day-over-day diff against `moveout_baseline.json`:
Output: `moveout_watch.json` + a printed ACTION NEEDED summary; baseline suppressed with `NO_BASELINE_WRITE=1` for a repeatable comparison.

rules.text: **Duplicate turns — prevented at the source, and a narrow daily mop-up (Lee Roy 2026-07-28).** The real fix for "a turn was created on a unit that was already turned" is the **creation guard**: the daily move-out scan (`pm_turn_dryrun.js`) treats a unit as already-serviced when a prior turn has **work that COMPLETED after the move-out date** — so it sets Rent Ready instead of creating a second turn. This is what stops new duplicates.
details: **Test COMPLETION, never the creation date (firm rule, Lee Roy 2026-07-30).** A turn is normally **created when notice is given — before the resident leaves — and executed after**, so a turn's creation date says nothing about which vacancy it belongs to. The only reliable signal is a meld's `completion_date` / `marked_complete` falling **after** the move-out. This is the same bright line the Rent Ready check uses ("was the unit actually turned since the move-out?").

**Two earlier versions of this rule were wrong — do not re-introduce either.** (1) "any completed turn created within ~75 days *before* the move-out" was too loose. (2) "a turn created *after* the move-out" is backwards and **created 3 duplicate turns in a single run on 2026-07-30** (kn47 K1 #M103, ps17 #A3, s129 #19 — each already serviced by a prior turn whose final walkthrough completed after the move-out); those were deleted the same day.
Note the mop-up below cannot cover this case: a brand-new OPEN turn duplicating a **CLOSED** one fails the "both still open" test, so duplicate prevention has to live in the creation guard.

`pm_dedupe_turns.js` (runs first in each turn workflow, before scheduling) is a deliberately **narrow** mop-up: it only neutralizes a **genuine current duplicate** — two turns for one unit that are **both still OPEN and created within 14 days** of each other (e.g. kn47 L205, created 3 days apart). It keeps the canonical one (most-complete → most-melds → earliest) and deletes the other's open melds + project.

It **never auto-deletes a COMPLETED turn.** A completed "duplicate" is ambiguous (could be a legitimate re-turn months later) and deleting its project would destroy completed-meld history. Two open turns created far apart (a stale abandoned turn + a fresh one) are also left alone — that's not a duplicate. Any historical completed-duplicate cleanup is a deliberate one-time human review, never the daily automation.

**The daily scan DOES catch a unit that didn't vacate / re-rented:** `pm_cancelled_turn_cleanup.js` (also first in each workflow) removes an OPEN turn whose unit is no longer vacant / on-notice in AppFolio. It intentionally skips turns with completed in-house work (never deletes finished work).
